questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a private board cannot direct a legislature to enact a rule.
questions.stem: Sky log entry: A colleague asks why an observatory board cannot simply order the county to build a darker-sky ordinance for the club's site.

options.text: Because only a legislature makes law, and a club board cannot direct how the county legislates
Because the county already spent public funds on the observatory and owes it further action
options.misconception: assumes prior public spending obliges the county

options.text: Because the nondelegation doctrine bars only federal agencies and leaves private clubs free
options.misconception: believes the doctrine reaches only federal agencies

options.text: Because a dark-sky ordinance would be a taking that no private organisation may request
options.misconception: treats any request for legislation as a taking

questions.explanation: Only a legislature may make law, so a club board cannot order a county to enact an ordinance. The tempting errors are that prior spending or the nondelegation doctrine licenses the demand.
questions.hint: Ask which body in the scenario holds lawmaking power.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.topic: Legal status of an executive order
questions.learningObjective: State what an executive order binds and what it cannot reach.

stimulus.body: A federal order titled 'Coordinating Federal Night-Sky Observations in Designated Dark-Sky Counties' directs agencies to consider a joint permitting timetable for observatories in three counties, and states that it creates no new obligation for any private observer.

questions.stem: Reading log note: I copied a federal order telling agencies to coordinate permitting for observatories; what legal weight should I give it?

options.text: It creates a binding schedule for every county hosting a dark-sky site, whether or not it agrees
options.misconception: assumes an order reaches states and private parties

options.text: It directs executive agencies internally and has no binding force on states or private observers
It is only a speech excerpt and carries no legal effect even on the agencies it names
options.misconception: treats every executive order as pure rhetoric

options.text: It becomes an enforceable regulation once agencies begin complying with it in practice
options.misconception: believes practice alone converts an order into a rule

questions.explanation: An executive order is a directive for the executive branch and binds no one outside it. The tempting errors are that publication or practice extends its reach, or that it is merely rhetorical.
questions.hint: Ask who the order speaks to.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: List the components of a complete rulemaking record.
questions.stem: Journal note: The club's lawyer asked me to explain in writing what makes a notice-and-comment rulemaking record complete, using the town's lighting rule as the example.

answer.exemplar: A complete notice-and-comment record shows that the agency published an adequately reasoned proposal stating its authority and the text of the proposed rule, that it received comments, and that it gave a reasoned response to each significant comment in the final rule.

questions.explanation: Rulemaking review looks at the whole record: proposal, comments, and response. Missing any piece lets a court ask whether the agency considered the important comments.
questions.hint: Name the three parts of a rulemaking record.

questions.topic: An interpretive rule beside a legislative rule
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish an explanatory document from a document that adds an escape from a rule.

stimulus.body: A county health department issued 'Guidance on Nighttime Lighting for Outdoor Cafes'. It says it 'explains and summarizes' existing ordinance provisions and 'does not impose new requirements'. It also says a cafe may deviate whenever 'practical considerations warrant'.

questions.stem: Cafe log note: A cafe told me it would ignore the light limits under the county guidance, citing the deviation sentence. Is that reading sound?

options.text: Yes, because the deviation sentence is part of the agency's interpretation of the ordinance
options.misconception: treats interpretive guidance as if it bound the agency

options.text: Yes, because any document labelled guidance must be read in the cafe's favour
options.misconception: assumes ambiguity is construed for the regulated party

options.text: No, because guidance cannot add a discretionary escape from a binding ordinance requirement
No, because the guidance is void in its entirety and every statement in it is worthless
options.misconception: concludes a vague guidance document has no force

questions.explanation: The guidance calls itself explanatory, so its deviation sentence cannot permit conduct the ordinance forbids. A regulated party gains no rights from a document the agency calls non-binding.
questions.hint: Ask whether the document claims to impose duties.

questions.learningObjective: Classify a document labelled a clarification and state the procedure it requires.
questions.stem: Sky log entry: Stage one, classify the new 'voluntary dark-sky certification procedure' as legislative or interpretive; stage two, say what that classification requires of the observatory.

options.text: It is interpretive, so the observatory may ignore it and keep using the earlier procedure
options.misconception: relies on the document's title rather than its effect

options.text: It is legislative, so the observatory may comply informally while the paperwork is finished
options.misconception: assumes a substantive rule binds before adoption ends

options.text: It is interpretive, so the observatory must follow the agency's current statement of the law
options.misconception: conflates interpretation with a binding requirement

options.text: It is legislative in substance, so notice and comment must precede any duty it imposes

questions.explanation: A label such as clarification does not control; if the document creates a new duty it is legislative and needs notice and comment. Treating the label as decisive is the tempting error.

questions.learningObjective: Explain why a memorandum cannot alter a regulation.
questions.stem: Weight log note: The state's transport secretary sent us a memorandum saying the vehicle weight rule for observatory trucks is being ignored, and a news report repeated it as a new legal requirement.

options.text: Because the memorandum comes from the secretary, it supersedes the regulation when they conflict
options.misconception: believes a senior official's memo overrides a rule

options.text: The press report makes the memorandum a public rule that the observatory must now comply with
options.misconception: treats press coverage as rulemaking

options.text: The memorandum cannot change the regulation, and repeating it in the press adds no legal force
Because the memorandum shows the rule is not enforced, the regulation is no longer in force
options.misconception: infers repeal from non-enforcement

questions.explanation: A memorandum communicates; it does not change a rule, and publicity adds no force. The tempting errors are that seniority or press coverage supplies legal force, or that non-enforcement repeals a rule.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Describe what congressional committee oversight can achieve.
questions.stem: Newsletter note: I drafted a paragraph for the club newsletter describing what congressional committee oversight can and cannot do about agency lighting rules.

answer.exemplar: Committee oversight is a supervisory tool: committees may investigate, hold hearings, and issue reports and recommendations that show how an agency carries out its statute. Oversight may expose unlawful conduct and build support for legislation, but it does not itself order the agency to change a rule or supply authority the agency lacks.

questions.explanation: Oversight informs and supervises; it does not command or repeal. A report that criticises an agency rule does not by itself change what the agency must do.
questions.hint: Separate the power to investigate from the power to command.

questions.topic: An agency acting beyond its statute

stimulus.body: Section 4(a) of the state Observatory Lighting Act directs the environmental agency to 'study and report to the legislature on the impacts of outdoor lighting on night-sky conditions'. The statute provides no rulemaking authority, no licensing power and no penalty authority.

questions.stem: Permit log note: The agency issued a rule requiring counties to obtain a lighting permit before approving any large car park. Can the statute support that?

options.text: No, because the statute authorises study and reporting only, and a permit requirement exceeds that grant
Yes, because a rule is a reasonable means to gather the facts the statute directs the agency to study
options.misconception: treats rulemaking as a way to gather information

options.text: Yes, because permitting is an obvious administrative tool an agency may use without express authority
options.misconception: assumes an agency may pick its own tools

options.text: Yes, because the statute's reference to impacts lets the agency adopt any measure that reduces them
options.misconception: reads general language as a blank cheque

questions.explanation: An agency may act only within the powers its statute confers, and a duty to study and report carries no permitting power. The tempting error is treating a sensible tool as an authorised one.
questions.hint: Compare the rule to the authority actually granted.

options.text: The requirement is law, because a governor's press release carries the force of an executive order
options.misconception: treats a press release as an executive order

options.text: The requirement is law, because the governor's signature substitutes for the legislature's assent
options.misconception: believes executive fiat replaces lawmaking

options.text: The requirement becomes law once the governor signs an executive order to the same effect
options.misconception: assumes any executive order creates binding duties

options.text: The certificate requirement is not law, because the governor's announcement cannot substitute for legislation

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.topic: Legal status of an executive order
questions.learningObjective: Place an executive order among the binding legal materials.
questions.stem: Lecturer note: A visiting lecturer asked me to write a short note on where an executive order fits among binding legal materials, for the society newsletter.

answer.exemplar: An executive order is a written directive issued by the President to the executive branch. It binds executive officials and agencies, and the same authority that issued it can revoke or amend it. It does not legislate for private parties, and where Congress has delegated no underlying authority, an order cannot supply it.

questions.explanation: Orders govern the executive branch itself and can be withdrawn by the issuer. The tempting error is treating an order as a statute or as something binding private observers.
questions.hint: Name who is bound and who may withdraw the order.

questions.learningObjective: Assess a final rule that adds requirements after comments close.

stimulus.body: The environmental agency published a proposed outdoor lighting rule with a preamble, regulatory text and a cost-benefit explanation. After comments closed, the final rule added a sentence that had not appeared in the proposal and imposed a longer compliance period than proposed.

questions.stem: Deadline note: The final rule added a sentence and a longer deadline that no comment addressed. What problem does that create?

options.text: There is no problem, because an agency may add any clarifying sentence once comments have closed
options.misconception: believes post-comment edits need no justification

options.text: The agency must explain the late additions or show they follow logically from what was proposed
The only problem is the longer deadline, since a compliance period may never be extended
options.misconception: assumes any change to a deadline is fatal by itself

options.text: The problem is procedural only and cannot affect validity if the agency calls the change minor
options.misconception: dismisses procedure as irrelevant to validity

questions.explanation: A final rule must rest on the proposal and the comments, so late additions need explanation. The tempting errors are that edits need no reason, that deadlines matter, or that procedure is irrelevant.
questions.hint: Compare the final rule with the proposal that was noticed.

questions.topic: An interpretive rule beside a legislative rule
questions.learningObjective: Classify a definitional clause and a command clause in one code.

stimulus.body: Section 12 of the state outdoor lighting code reads: 'For purposes of this section, a shielded luminaire means one that emits no light above the horizontal plane.' Section 15 reads: 'Public agencies shall install shielded luminaires at all parking facilities within the state.'

questions.stem: Code note: One code section defines a shielded luminaire and another tells agencies what to install. Which is which?

options.text: Both sections are interpretive because both define how the code should be read before any duty arises
options.misconception: treats every definitional clause as interpretive

options.text: The definition supplies meaning and is interpretive; the installation duty is legislative
Both sections are legislative because together they establish what agencies must do at parking facilities
options.misconception: judges a clause by the document it sits in

options.text: The definition is legislative because it sets a technical standard; the duty section is interpretive
options.misconception: confuses a definitional limit with a command

questions.explanation: A definition supplies meaning; a command imposes an obligation. The tempting error is judging each clause by the label of the code or by the duty sitting next to it.
questions.hint: Ask whether the clause imposes a duty or supplies meaning.

questions.learningObjective: Classify a new requirement and state when it binds.
questions.stem: Timing note: Stage one, decide whether the new 'rooftop sensor requirement' is a legislative rule or an interpretation; stage two, say what the observatory must do before it is subject to it.

options.text: It is interpretive, so the observatory must follow the agency's view even before any rule is adopted
options.misconception: treats a draft interpretation as immediately binding

options.text: It is legislative, so the observatory must comply now because the agency says it takes effect at once
options.misconception: believes agency notice of effectiveness bypasses adoption

options.text: It is legislative, so no duty attaches until notice and comment are finished and the rule is adopted
It is interpretive, so nothing changes and the old rooftop sensors may stay in use
options.misconception: assumes interpretation has no effect on conduct

questions.explanation: A requirement imposing a new duty is legislative whatever it is called, and it binds only after notice and comment. The tempting error is treating a draft or an interpretation as already binding.
questions.hint: Substance first, then the procedural requirement.

options.text: Because it says shall, the note imposes a duty on the public exactly as a regulation would
options.misconception: confuses mandatory phrasing with legal effect

options.text: Because agency lawyers wrote it, the note carries the same authority as the statute funding the agency
options.misconception: equates staff instructions with statutory authority

options.text: Because it was issued in writing, it counts as a legislative rule without any further procedure
options.misconception: treats written form as rulemaking

options.text: An internal note binds agency staff only; it has no legal force over the public until adopted as a rule

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Contrast committee oversight with the exercise of legislative power.
questions.stem: Meeting note: I was asked at the society meeting to explain, in a few sentences, why committee oversight differs from the exercise of legislative power.

answer.exemplar: Oversight is the committee's watchfulness over how an agency carries out the law it administers: it investigates, holds hearings, questions officials and reports to the chamber. Legislative power makes law or withholds funds. Because oversight does not itself enact, repeal or command anything, a committee report can expose a problem and recommend a fix, but it cannot change the agency's statutory duties.

questions.explanation: Oversight is inquiry and report, not command or enactment. The tempting error is treating a critical committee report as though it had already amended the agency's statute.
questions.hint: Ask what the committee ends up producing.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the defect in guidance made immediately effective.

stimulus.body: A letter to the county surveyor states: 'The Department has issued temporary guidance establishing 500-foot setbacks for any observatory structure exceeding 40 feet in height. The guidance is effective immediately and will remain in effect until further notice.'

questions.stem: Letter note: The letter states the guidance is effective immediately. What legal problem does that create?

options.text: Immediate effect without notice and comment turns the document into an invalid rule, not mere guidance
No problem, because an agency may act at once when the statute moves on a short timeline
options.misconception: assumes urgency alone justifies skipping procedure

options.text: No problem, because the letter is addressed to a government office and not to the public
options.misconception: thinks the audience changes the procedural duty

options.text: The only problem is that until further notice is vague, and the vagueness is the whole defect
options.misconception: reduces the defect to drafting rather than procedure

questions.explanation: A document that imposes new duties and takes effect at once is legislative in substance and needs notice and comment. The tempting errors are urgency, audience, and drafting complaints that miss the defect.
questions.hint: Ask whether new duties began without notice.

questions.learningObjective: Explain why signing as an agent confers no lawmaking power.
questions.stem: Petition note: The club wanted the county to adopt a lighting code; the club's president signed a form 'acting as agent of the state' after reading the statute.

options.text: Private members cannot exercise a state's lawmaking power, and signing as an agent does not confer it
Signing as an agent lets the club exercise delegated state authority if the members are qualified voters
options.misconception: believes voter status supplies delegated power

options.text: The signature makes the form binding because the statute lets any resident file rules on lighting
options.misconception: reads a filing provision as a grant of authority

options.text: The club can exercise the power if the members ratify the form at a general meeting of the society
options.misconception: thinks internal ratification creates state power

questions.explanation: Lawmaking power is vested in government, not private associations, and self-description as an agent changes nothing. Voter status, a filing clause or internal ratification supplies no power.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.topic: Legal status of an executive order
questions.learningObjective: Contrast an executive order with an executive agreement.
questions.stem: Member note: A member asked me to describe in writing the difference between an executive order and an executive agreement, using a park lighting accord as an example.

answer.exemplar: An executive order is a unilateral written directive issued by the President directing the executive branch, and it is law only to the extent it rests on delegated statutory authority and affects the government itself. An executive agreement is a compact between the United States and a foreign state or international body, made under the President's treaty-making and agreement powers, and it creates international obligations rather than domestic rules.

questions.explanation: Orders speak to the executive branch; agreements bind the nation internationally and are not agency rules. The tempting error is treating an international accord as an internal directive.
questions.hint: Ask who is bound by each instrument.

questions.learningObjective: Read the rulemaking record to test the premise of a comment.

stimulus.body: A commenter wrote: 'The notice never mentions the cost of replacing unshielded fixtures, so the agency could not have considered it.' The agency replied: 'The notice states the number of affected fixtures and the estimated replacement cost per unit, and the final rule adopts a phase-in period drawn from that material.'

questions.stem: Comment note: The commenter says the notice was silent on replacement cost. How should the record be read?

options.text: The commenter's objection must be honoured because the agency cannot rely on its own summary
options.misconception: presumes every commenter is right regardless of the record

options.text: The record places the cost material in the notice, so the commenter's premise fails on its face
The record is silent, since the agency said the material was in a file not mentioned in the notice
options.misconception: assumes supporting files sit outside the record

options.text: The issue is irrelevant, because a comment that is factually wrong is disregarded in all cases
options.misconception: believes false comments need no response at all

questions.explanation: The record is read as a whole, and the agency's response explains where the material appeared. The tempting error is to treat a commenter's assertion as proof, or to excuse any response.
questions.hint: Read the notice and the agency's response together.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Explain what a committee accomplishes at a hearing on a rule.
questions.stem: Bulletin note: I was asked to write out, in plain words, what a legislative committee can accomplish in a hearing on an agency's lighting rule.

answer.exemplar: In a hearing a committee can question officials about how the rule was developed, what evidence supports it, and how the agency intends to enforce it. It can require documents and records, and it can use what it learns to build a report, a letter or a recommendation. A committee cannot in the hearing itself withdraw the rule, approve it, or substitute a different rule for the agency to follow.

questions.explanation: A hearing produces information and pressure, not legal change. The tempting error is treating questions at a hearing as approval, withdrawal or substitution of the rule.

questions.learningObjective: Describe the reasoned explanation a final rule must contain.
questions.stem: Pressure note: I drafted a paragraph for the club bulletin describing what a court wants to see in the explanation an agency gives for a rule.

answer.exemplar: A court wants the final rule to show the path from the proposal to the result: the authority relied on, the problems the agency found, the comments received and the reasons for the changes made, and an explanation of any new requirement or response to a significant comment that did not appear in the proposal. The explanation must be reasoned rather than conclusory.

questions.explanation: The explanation must connect the proposal to the result, not merely announce it. The tempting error is accepting conclusory statements as a reasoned response to significant comments.
questions.hint: Ask how the rule connects back to the proposal.

options.text: The regulation is outdated, so the later agency interpretation implicitly amends it
options.misconception: treats an interpretation as a silent amendment

questions.explanation: An interpretation fills gaps; it cannot contradict the text it explains. The tempting errors are that agency view controls, that both readings may be chosen, or that interpretation silently amends.

options.text: It is interpretive, because offices are only explaining how they will treat shielded installations

It is a rule, and it is invalid because the notice skipped notice and comment

questions.explanation: A new operative test is legislative in substance and the heading is not decisive. The tempting errors are trusting the agency's account of its practice, ignoring the change, or taking the label as settled.

options.misconception: treats a report as rulemaking

options.misconception: denies the memo any persuasive value

options.text: A policy memo states the agency's position and creates no enforceable duty for anyone outside it

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish committee oversight from rulemaking participation.
questions.stem: Archive note: I wrote a short note for the archive explaining what committee oversight adds that a public hearing on a rule does not.

answer.exemplar: A public hearing on a rule collects comments for the rulemaker and feeds the rulemaking record. Committee oversight does something different: it aims at supervising how an agency carries out the law, and it answers to the wider chamber rather than to the rule. A committee may hold hearings, request documents and report publicly, and the publicity and political accountability are what make it distinct from rulemaking.

questions.explanation: A rule hearing builds the record for the agency; oversight looks past the rule at the agency's conduct. The tempting error is treating both as the same kind of participation.
questions.hint: Ask who each process is accountable to.

options.misconception: treats signature as statutory authority

options.misconception: expands a defined class by analogy

questions.explanation: The order cannot enlarge the class the statute covers, whatever the necessity. The tempting errors are that necessity or signature supplies authority, or that a government body counts as an operator.

options.misconception: treats adoption of private standards as rulemaking

options.misconception: assumes unenforced directives have legal force

options.misconception: treats subject headings as adequate responses

options.text: Only a count of comments, since a numerical summary satisfies the response requirement
options.misconception: thinks a comment tally answers comments

options.misconception: lets the agency define its own authority

options.text: The note is interpretive, because it only applies to applications for the agency's own permits
options.misconception: judges scope rather than legal effect

options.text: The note is a rule, and it is valid because the agency said its interpretation was binding
options.misconception: treats the agency's assertion as the test for validity

options.text: A binding-sounding interpretation that adds a requirement is legislative, whatever the note asserts

questions.explanation: Character turns on effect, not self-description. The tempting errors are that the agency defines its own authority, that scope matters more than effect, or that its assertion validates it.

questions.learningObjective: Explain what changes when an agency relabels a new requirement.
questions.stem: Labels note: I drafted a note for the archive on what changes when an agency labels a new reporting requirement a clarification.

answer.exemplar: Nothing changes in law when the label changes, because the character of a document follows its effect. A requirement that imposes a new duty, however it is titled, is a legislative rule and must go through notice and comment before it binds anyone. Calling the same document a clarification does not remove the duty it creates and does not excuse the procedure; it only makes the defect harder to see.

questions.explanation: Labels do not move a document between the categories; its effect does. The tempting error is that a chosen title can excuse the procedure that the substance requires.
questions.hint: Judge the requirement, not the title.

options.misconception: assumes internal documents have no legal effect

options.misconception: focuses on signatory authority alone

options.misconception: makes enforcement depend on a request

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Explain what tools a private organisation actually holds.
questions.stem: Strategy note: I wrote a short explanation of what a club cannot do, even with the best arguments and a sympathetic cause.

answer.exemplar: A private organisation cannot make law, bind other private parties, or compel a public body to act, however strong its reasons. Its proper tools are persuasion, coalition, petitioning the body that holds the power, litigation where a legal right is being violated, and organised comment on rules that affect it. Claiming a power the organisation lacks is not a way of winning; it invites the body to dismiss the rest of what it says.

questions.explanation: Persuasion and the lawful tools are what private groups have; the power to bind does not come with a good cause. The tempting error is believing a strong argument confers a legal power.
questions.hint: Ask what instrument the organisation actually holds.

options.misconception: assumes all proclamations bind agencies

options.text: It creates a duty for federal agencies and for any entity that receives a federal grant
options.misconception: extends proclamation duties to grant recipients

It has no effect of any kind, because a proclamation cannot even influence agency practice
options.misconception: denies proclamations any practical influence

questions.explanation: A document that asks rather than commands and disclaims obligation creates none. The tempting errors are that every proclamation binds agencies, that grants extend it, or that it has no influence.
questions.hint: Read the operative verbs in the document.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: State the limits on what a memorandum may do to a regulation.
questions.stem: Memorandum note: I drafted a note for the archive on what a memorandum may and may not do to an existing regulation.

answer.exemplar: A memorandum is a communication to staff or to the public about how an agency understands or intends to apply a regulation. It may inform, instruct personnel and organise the agency's internal practice. It may not create new legal obligations for regulated parties, and it may not contradict the regulation it discusses. Where a memorandum departs from the regulation's meaning, the regulation controls and the memorandum supplies no defence.

questions.explanation: A memo informs and organises; it cannot add duties or override the text it describes. The tempting error is treating a memo as a source of rights or as a way around the regulation.
questions.hint: Ask whether the memo adds duties for anyone.

options.misconception: dismisses committee findings as legally inert

questions.explanation: Oversight produces visibility and recommendation, not commands. The tempting errors treat findings as law, treat the funding threat as a duty, or dismiss the report as legally irrelevant.
questions.hint: Separate the report's persuasion from its legal force.

questions.learningObjective: Contrast a rule of presidential conduct with an executive order.
questions.stem: Conduct note: I wrote a short note explaining what a rule of presidential conduct on lighting reviews differs from an executive order.

answer.exemplar: A rule of presidential conduct is a statement of internal practice, discipline and expectation for the President and senior officials; it is directed inward and is not a source of legal authority for anyone else. The practical difference is that conduct rules shape conduct within the office, while orders change what agencies and officials must do.

questions.explanation: Conduct rules look inward; orders direct outward. The tempting error is treating a statement of presidential practice as a legal directive with external effect.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Classify an internal memo that interprets a regulation.

stimulus.body: A memo to the agency's own programme staff reads: 'For administrative convenience, staff should treat a facility's shade structures as not being outdoor lighting facilities for purposes of the regulations until the agency issues further guidance. Staff should not treat this instruction as a change in the regulations themselves.'

questions.stem: Practice note: The memo tells staff to ignore part of the regulation but says it is not a change. What is its legal character?

options.text: It is a legislative rule that changes the regulation, because it alters what facilities must do
options.misconception: ignores the memo's own characterisation

options.text: An instruction explaining the regulation without contradicting it is interpretive guidance
It is an ultra vires act, because no agency may ever narrow its own regulation
options.misconception: assumes all narrowing is unlawful

options.text: It binds private facilities, because staff applying it will do so in every permit decision
options.misconception: confuses practical effect with legal force

questions.explanation: Guidance explaining the regulation without contradicting it is interpretive. The tempting errors are recharacterising it as a rule, calling all narrowing ultra vires, or equating practice with legal force.
questions.hint: Compare the memo's instruction with the regulation it names.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Explain what committee inaction does not establish.
questions.stem: Inaction note: A club member claimed that because the committee held no hearings on the agency's rule, the committee must have approved it.

options.text: Yes, because committees approve by silence when they take no action within the session
options.misconception: treats silence as affirmative approval

options.text: Yes, because a committee's failure to object shows the rule met the standard of review
options.misconception: confuses inaction with a merits judgment

options.text: No, because silence and inaction in committee are not approval and prove nothing
Yes, because committee silence excuses the agency from the notice-and-comment requirement
options.misconception: claims committee inaction removes procedure

questions.explanation: Inaction is not approval and never supplies missing procedure. The tempting errors are silence as assent, silence as a merits ruling, and silence as a substitute for the agency's process.
questions.hint: Absence of action proves nothing was approved.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.topic: An agency acting beyond its statute
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish an agency's power to act from its power to demand information.
questions.stem: Reporting note: I drafted a short explanation of the difference between an agency's power to act and its power to require information from regulated parties.

answer.exemplar: An agency's power to act must come from a grant in its statute, and a statute authorising it to regulate in a field generally lets it act within that field and no more. The power to demand information is narrower and usually needs a clearer grant, such as express inspection or reporting authority, because information demands burden private parties and build a record. Courts therefore test reporting conditions against the specific wording of the grant.

questions.explanation: Acting power and information power are different grants, and information demands are tested strictly. The tempting error is that general regulatory authority always includes power to demand reports.
questions.hint: Read the specific grant for inspection or reporting.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Decide when a delegation of rulemaking power is valid.
questions.stem: Delegation note: Stage one, decide whether the legislature may delegate to the Department the power to decide when a private landowner must dim lights; stage two, say what that permits.

options.text: Any delegation is void, so the Department may not set any rule about lighting at all
options.misconception: treats every delegation as invalid

options.text: A delegation is void unless the legislature itself approves each rule the Department writes
options.misconception: requires legislative approval of each rule

options.text: A delegation is void because only the legislature may decide what counts as an excessive light level
options.misconception: confuses level-setting with value judgment

options.text: A delegation is valid when the legislature sets limits and the agency rules within them

questions.explanation: A delegation is valid when the legislature sets limits and the agency rules within them. The tempting errors are that all delegation is void, that each rule needs approval, or that only lawmakers may judge levels.
questions.hint: Ask whether the legislature set the governing limits.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.topic: Legal status of an executive order
questions.learningObjective: Identify what an order directing a report does not do.

stimulus.body: An executive order states: 'Federal agencies shall, in coordination with state and local authorities, prepare a report on the effects of artificial light on migratory birds at night. Each agency shall determine the scope of its own contribution within the framework described below.'

questions.stem: Order note: The order asks federal agencies to prepare a report and coordinate with states. What does it not do?

options.text: It does not require any agency to do anything, because preparing a report is a voluntary courtesy
options.misconception: treats a directive as optional

options.text: It does not itself bind states or private observatories, and it does not prescribe how agencies must act
It does not create any reporting burden on agencies, since agencies may refuse to coordinate
options.misconception: assumes agencies may refuse a directive

options.text: It does not survive beyond the current administration, because orders always expire with the presidency
options.misconception: assumes all orders expire automatically

questions.explanation: An order directs executive agencies but binds no state or private observer, and leaves method to them. The tempting errors are that a directive is optional, agencies may refuse it, or all orders lapse.
questions.hint: Ask which actors the order actually reaches.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.learningObjective: Assess a final rule that drops a noticed provision without explanation.

stimulus.body: The agency's notice asked for comment on 'proposed reporting requirements for observatories receiving state grants', including the form of the report, the frequency, and the consequences of late filing. The final rule adopted the form and frequency but dropped the consequences provision entirely, without explaining the change.

questions.stem: Dropping note: The final rule dropped a provision that was noticed, without explanation. What does that raise?

options.text: Nothing, because an agency may always narrow its own proposal without explanation
options.misconception: assumes narrowing is always free

options.text: Nothing, because commenters objected to the consequences provision and the agency was entitled to drop it
options.misconception: infers a reason that was never stated

options.text: The unexplained change may undercut the reasoned basis the record must show for what was adopted
The rule is void, because any provision noticed but not adopted makes the whole rule invalid
options.misconception: makes one change void the entire rule

questions.explanation: A final rule must be supported by the record, and an unexplained change weakens that support. The tempting errors are that narrowing is free, that a reason may be supplied later, or that the rule falls entirely.
questions.hint: Ask whether the final rule rests on the record as made.

questions.subject: US_GOVERNMENT
questions.topic: An interpretive rule beside a legislative rule
questions.learningObjective: Decide whether a general mandate supports a new private reporting duty.
questions.stem: Mandate note: The agency's statute told it to 'promote the preservation of the night sky', and the agency then required every private observatory to install brightness sensors.

options.text: The mandate supports the duty, because the agency may use any reasonable means to achieve its purpose
options.misconception: grants unlimited means to pursue a purpose

options.text: The mandate supports the duty, because observing the night sky is an activity the agency may regulate
options.misconception: treats a related subject as authority

options.text: The mandate supports the duty, because collecting data is always a permissible intermediate step
options.misconception: assumes data collection is always permitted

options.text: An interpretive reading of a general mandate cannot itself create a private reporting duty the statute omits

questions.explanation: A general mandate to promote a goal does not authorise private obligations; the statute must grant the power. The tempting errors are unlimited means, subject-matter jurisdiction, and blanket permission to collect data.
questions.hint: Ask whether the statute creates the duty it enforces.
